meta.scope: Mexico batch 12 — Two poorest/most marginalized states (Chiapas & Guerrero) mapped with the same hierarchy: State entity → Metro/capital → Key municipalities → Local institute / judiciary / IMSS / CNGMD / Economic Census. Purpose: test statistical homogeneity across rich vs poor Mexico.
meta.homogeneity_finding: The hierarchy exists on paper everywhere, but independent local statistical production is markedly thinner in Chiapas and Guerrero. Most usable series remain national INEGI cuts. Local institutes (CEIEG Chiapas) often compile rather than originate. Judicial and municipal data are present via national censuses but lack the rich local yearbooks and dashboards seen in CDMX, Jalisco or Nuevo León.

candidates.title: Chiapas (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.publisher: INEGI + CEIEG Chiapas + Gobierno de Chiapas
candidates.description: Poorest state by multidimensional poverty (66.0% in 2024) and extreme poverty (27.1%). Large indigenous population, predominantly rural. Statistical capacity exists but is thinner and more dependent on national INEGI programmes than northern or central states.
candidates.notes: Highest multidimensional poverty (66.0%) and extreme poverty (27.1%) in the 2024 INEGI measurement. Tests whether the State → Metro → Municipality → Local institute hierarchy survives under extreme poverty and marginalization. Local CEIEG products are frequently compilations of INEGI data.

candidates.title: Tuxtla Gutiérrez — capital / limited metro statistical profile
candidates.description: Capital and principal urban centre of Chiapas. Functions as the limited ‘metro’ node for the state. Data almost entirely from national programmes (census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census) with thinner independent local statistical production than IIEG Jalisco or IPDP CDMX.
referenced_by: CEIEG compilations of INEGI poverty data
candidates.notes: In the poorest state the ‘metro’ node is essentially the capital city. Local statistical capacity is weaker; most usable series remain national programmes cut to state or municipality.

candidates.title: Comité Estatal de Información Estadística y Geográfica de Chiapas (CEIEG)
candidates.description: State-level statistical coordination body. Produces or compiles poverty, social and geographic information, but with thinner independent primary-survey cadence than IIEG Jalisco or IPDP CDMX.
candidates.notes: Homogeneity test: the local statistical institute exists but produces fewer original recurring primary surveys. Heavy dependence on INEGI national programmes is visible. Poverty reports are often re-compilations of INEGI ENIGH / multidimensional poverty results.

candidates.title: Guerrero (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Second-poorest state by multidimensional poverty (58.1% in 2024) and extreme poverty (21.3%). High marginalization, indigenous population, insecurity and weak local statistical infrastructure relative to northern or central states.
candidates.notes: Deliberate contrast case. 58.1% multidimensional poverty and 21.3% extreme poverty (2024). Tests whether the State → Metro → Municipality → Local institute hierarchy survives in a high-poverty, high-marginalization, high-insecurity environment.

candidates.title: Acapulco de Juárez — municipal / nominal metro profile
candidates.description: Principal urban centre and nominal ‘metro’ node for Guerrero. Tourism-dependent economy repeatedly affected by hurricanes and high insecurity. Statistical presence is almost entirely national programmes (census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census, tourism indicators) with limited independent local statistical production.
candidates.notes: In the second-poorest state the main urban node has thin independent statistical capacity. Hurricane recovery and insecurity further disrupt continuous local data production. Most usable numbers remain national cuts. Clear contrast with Zapopan or CDMX alcaldías.

candidates.title: Poder Judicial / Fiscalía del Estado de Guerrero — statistical presence
candidates.publisher: Poder Judicial del Estado de Guerrero / Fiscalía General del Estado
candidates.description: State justice and prosecution institutions. Data appear mainly through national CNIJE / CNPJE rather than rich independent local yearbooks.
candidates.notes: Homogeneity test: in a high-poverty, high-insecurity state the local judicial statistical production is thin. Most usable numbers come from the national INEGI justice censuses rather than a robust independent state judicial statistical office.

candidates.title: Chiapas (entidad federativa) — full hierarchy test node
candidates.description: Poorest state (66.0% multidimensional poverty, 27.1% extreme poverty in 2024). Explicit test of whether the State → Metro → Municipality → Local institute hierarchy exists under extreme marginalization.
candidates.notes: Highest poverty rates in the country. Local CEIEG exists but independent primary-survey capacity is thin; many ‘state’ reports are compilations of INEGI data.

candidates.title: Tuxtla Gutiérrez — capital municipal profile (Chiapas)
candidates.description: Capital and principal urban centre of the poorest state. Functions as the limited metro node. Data almost entirely from national programmes with thinner independent local statistical production.
referenced_by: National census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census
CEIEG compilations of INEGI poverty data
candidates.notes: In the poorest state the capital still relies overwhelmingly on INEGI national programmes. Local statistical capacity is thinner than IIEG Jalisco or IPDP CDMX.

candidates.title: Guerrero (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity (poverty contrast)
candidates.description: Second-poorest state (58.1% multidimensional poverty, 21.3% extreme poverty in 2024). High marginalization, indigenous population, insecurity and weaker local statistical infrastructure.
candidates.notes: Deliberate contrast case to Nuevo León, Jalisco and CDMX. Tests homogeneity of the statistical hierarchy under high poverty and insecurity.

candidates.title: Acapulco de Juárez — municipal / nominal metro profile (Guerrero)
candidates.description: Principal urban centre and nominal metro node for Guerrero. Tourism-dependent, repeatedly affected by hurricanes and high insecurity. Statistical presence almost entirely from national programmes; limited independent local statistical production.
referenced_by: National census, ENOE, ENIGH, CNGMD, economic census
candidates.notes: In the second-poorest state the main urban node has thin independent statistical capacity. Hurricane recovery and insecurity disrupt continuous local data. Most usable numbers remain national cuts. Clear contrast with Zapopan or CDMX alcaldías.
